top_stories.title: Strategy Sets New Bitcoin Holdings Record
points: Strategy now holds 9,240 Bitcoin, exceeding all previous holdings records for the company.
The accumulation reflects a deliberate long-term strategy positioning Bitcoin as a core corporate treasury asset.
Large institutional holdings like this reduce available market supply, potentially supporting price floors.
Institutional adoption by established financial firms is seen as validating the maturation of crypto as an asset class.

unique_angles.point: Strategy is separately seeking shareholder approval for daily dividend accrual on STRC and three other preferred stocks, aiming to attract income investors and restore STRC's price toward its $100 par value (it has traded below that since May).

items.title: Bitget $388M Exploit Recovery
points: Roughly $388 million was drained from Bitget's hot and warm wallets on September 24, the largest reported crypto theft of 2026; attackers exploited a vulnerability in a third-party security product to obtain credentials and bypass risk controls.
Withdrawals are resuming in phases: BTC and ETH resumed September 29, USDT on September 30, with all remaining assets and fiat available by October 2.
User balances and cold (offline) wallets were unaffected; Bitget's 5,500 BTC User Protection Fund will fully cover customer losses.
Bitget suspects a sophisticated, state-backed attacker, pointing to North Korea as the likely source.

items.title: Ethereum's 'Cryptographic World Computer' Vision
points: Vitalik Buterin's new paper repositions Ethereum as a hybrid architecture combining traditional blockchain consensus with modern cryptography (using mathematical proofs to enable trustless computation) rather than being a pure blockchain.
The roadmap includes FOCIL (a mechanism for censorship resistance), EIP-8288, 'Lean consensus,' state management improvements, and mempool upgrades including transaction privacy.
Obfuscation (a cryptographic technique for hiding data while still proving computation correctness) is floated as a longer-term primitive to expand on-chain computation.
The paper compares how Bitcoin and Ethereum's design goals have diverged from their 2015 origins through 2025, with projections to 2030.

items.title: Solana's Alpenglow Finality Breakthrough
points: Solana's Alpenglow upgrade has moved to public testnet, replacing the old TowerBFT consensus with a new 'Votor' protocol that cuts transaction finality (the point transactions become irreversible) from 12.8 seconds to 150 milliseconds.

Votor replaces on-chain vote accumulation with direct validator-to-validator messaging that settles in one or two rounds; it requires Agave 4.3 software, and the Firedancer and Frankendancer clients don't yet support it.
Faster finality could shorten exchange deposit hold times, cross-chain bridge wait periods, and merchant payment confirmation delays.
Mainnet deployment is tentatively targeted for September 28 but not yet confirmed.

items.title: Circle's USDC Off-Ramp Strategy via Tazapay
points: Circle's acquisition of Tazapay (announced September 8) primarily targets the Singapore-based B2B payments firm's existing USDC redemption volume rather than future growth potential.
About one-third of Tazapay's payout business is already funded in USDC, up from under 10% in June, with monthly redemptions hitting $562 million in the first 25 days of September.
The real profit center is the FX spread at the fiat off-ramp (converting stablecoin to local currency), not the blockchain layer; Tazapay earns only 2 basis points (0.02%) of revenue on-chain.
Tazapay's product flow is one-directional (stablecoin in, fiat out) via Circle Mint, making the deal a play to capture high-volume off-ramp economics rather than on-chain innovation.
